chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: Why being a musician meant being somebody
summary: He says musicians were celebrated, women and dance-givers came to them, and playing meant a happy life until stranded on the road.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: instruments, there come the women, there come the people, and you see the people giving the dances, offering you something -- and you're celebrated. And it's human nature to want to be somebody. So here was a chance for you to get a little exposure and to be somebody and to make a living -- and it's fun. Because I noticed right away, when I wanted to...getting my mind set to be a musician, every day you're going somewhere where people are having fun. Everywhere you go to play, it's people having...

Yeah. And it's a happy life you're living. Until you start to get stranded when you get out on the road. Even then, your life isn't (?). They want you to get out, don't hang around. So you see these people, and you look at them, and they're talking about you. It's like you see Ted Williams or Jackie Robinson or Ty Cobb, speaking in baseball like a reference...
